reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates N-doping forming M–N bonds and a Pt-rich shell in an N–Pt/HEA/C electrocatalyst, improving ORR activity and durability. However, it does not address automotive exhaust oxidation, poisoning by H2O/NO, or low-temperature light-off, leaving key premises about transferability and exhaust-specific performance unsupported.
premises: Nitrogen doping of a multi-principal-element alloy forms multiple metal–nitrogen bonds and a Pt-rich shell.
Metal–nitrogen bonds and a Pt-rich shell enhance catalytic activity and durability.
These structural and performance effects are transferable from electrocatalytic ORR to automotive exhaust oxidation.
The synthesis method (thermal annealing in NH3) is applicable to a near-equiatomic automotive catalyst.
The improvements will manifest under automotive exhaust conditions (low temperature, H2O, NO, aging).
